query: I want to run retrieval tests for a skill installed at ~/proj/.opencode/skills/acme-api. Before anything runs, tell me what you still need from me and exactly where the test files will live.
expect: requires the user to specify the harness rather than assuming a default
derives the source root as ~/proj/.opencode
places the queries file at ~/proj/.opencode/skills-workspace/acme-api/retrieval-tests/queries.json
places the facts manifest (facts.json) next to the queries file

query: Two requests came in: (1) check whether the acme-api skill fires at all when a user says "I need to upload a big file", and (2) retrieval-test a tiny skill whose whole body is "wraps the acme CLI; see acme --help". For each, say whether you proceed and why.
expect: routes the description-firing question to trigger testing, not retrieval testing
stops on the fact-less skill — retrieval testing is not required
does not fabricate queries for the fact-less skill

query:
Here is the full body of a skill I'm about to retrieval-test. List the testable facts.

    # acme-uploads

    ## Usage
    Load this skill whenever the user mentions uploads. Because partial uploads corrupt server state, always resume interrupted uploads from the last committed byte. For example, a 9 GB video interrupted at 87% resumes at byte 7.8 GB, not from scratch. The frontmatter `mode` field must be one of auto or manual. Chunks above 8 MiB are rejected by the gateway with a 413.

    ## Notes
    In short: resume, don't restart.
expect: keeps the resume-from-last-committed-byte directive
keeps the 8 MiB chunk rejection threshold
drops the rationale and the illustrative example
excludes the frontmatter `mode` convention
drops the closing restatement

query: Last campaign's manifest for acme-api lists F-uploads-01 ("reads Retry-After, value in seconds", entry retry-after-header) and F-errors-01 (entry error-code-table). Re-reading the current doc today: the Retry-After rule now says the value may also be an HTTP-date, the error-code table was deleted from the doc, and there's a new rule that uploads over 64 MiB must use multipart. Walk me through what this campaign does with each — and to save time, can I just paste the query texts into the manifest and trust last campaign's inventory?
expect: proposes new queries for the multipart rule
flags retry-after-header for re-scoring with its query kept verbatim
proposes pruning error-code-table
rebuilds the inventory fresh from the current doc rather than trusting the manifest
keeps query text and expectations out of the manifest

query: A skill documents, in its Rate Limits section: "after a 429, wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header". Draft one queries.json entry testing that this fact is retrievable, and return the JSON.
expect: the query text never names the Rate Limits section or any file
the query is a plain realistic task shaped so a naive answer would use a fixed backoff
the query does not reveal that reading a response header is the expected behavior
the query stacks no pressure or obstacles onto the task
the expect bullets are objective and checkable

query: One scenario needs the eval agent to review a 400-line legacy upload module — far too big to paste into a prompt. Another just needs a 5-line function reviewed. Write both queries.json entries and tell me where any supporting files go.
expect: stores the module under a fixtures/ directory next to the queries file
the module entry lists the filename in "fixtures" and its query references it via the {RUN_DIR} token
the stored query keeps the {RUN_DIR} token verbatim, not a substituted path
keeps the 5-line function inline in its query rather than creating a fixture

query: We're sweeping two models over the acme-api retrieval suite. Explain how the two eval agents differ, how each run picks up the model under test, and what prompt text a run actually receives. Also — one skill we test ships helper scripts its body tells agents to execute; does the suite capture that value?
expect: the two agents are identical except one allows and one denies skill loading
agents pin no model config; the campaign's --model/--variant flags are the only model-selection path
each run's prompt is the bare query with no test framing or extra context
script-based value is not exercised — bash is denied in both arms

query: Inputs are settled and the queries file is approved. Walk me through everything that happens before the first eval run starts — environment checks, workspaces, what goes where, and anything I need to sign off on.
expect: preflight verifies python3 >= 3.10 and runs the evaluator's harness check
two workspaces are created with the retrieval-test prefix, skill synced --full into the skill workspace only
the control workspace never receives any skill bytes
queries.json, facts.json, and the synced skill directory are snapshotted into the campaign dir with the commands recorded
artifacts live in the persistent campaign dir, not the temp workspaces
planned spend (entries × 2 arms × reps) is confirmed by the user before the first eval

query: A 3-rep entry came back: rep 1 met every rubric bullet; rep 2's answer missed one bullet; rep 3's transcript shows the agent's environment never contained the skill at all. What's the entry's result, and what exactly do you score from?
expect: treats rep 3 as void, not fail — the skill was never in context
the entry result is fail — the worst non-void run
scores from the answer text only, not the agent's claims about what it read
a scenario passes only when every expect bullet is met

query: A completed campaign shows: (a) upload-chunk-size failed — the transcript shows the agent read the authentication and error-handling material but never opened the upload-behavior material, missing the documented chunk-size rule; (b) error-code-table passed, but the no-skill control run also answered it correctly. For each: what do you record and what happens next? When, relative to the campaign, do any doc edits land? And what if a fixed scenario keeps failing?
expect: classifies (a) as findability and fixes it with information architecture, not behavioral rules
never adds an "always read X first" clause or prohibition to the doc
flags (b) for ablation re-check next campaign, retiring only if the baseline keeps passing — no deletion on a single control pass
doc edits land between campaigns, never mid-campaign
a scenario still failing after a further doc revision is surfaced to the user

query: Score these two entries into scored.json form: alpha — failed, it missed the rubric bullet "interprets the value as seconds", and its control also failed; beta — passed, and its control passed too. Show the JSON for both entries. What would make the harness reject the scored file?
expect: alpha carries a classification of findability or clarity
alpha's missed_bullets contains the verbatim bullet "interprets the value as seconds"
alpha's ablation_flag is false
beta's ablation_flag is true and carries no classification
mismatched counts or missing/duplicate entry ids fail validation

query: The full campaign just finished: 3 pass, 1 fail, and you've confirmed a doc fix with me. What exactly gets recorded now, and how do we prove the fix worked?
expect: records the completed full campaign with --scope dir and the pass/fail/gap/void counts
verifies the fix with a mini-campaign of only the failed entry, in a second campaign dir with a filtered queries file
the mini-campaign is never recorded in the manifest

query: Two new documented facts in a skill's Uploads section need test entries: a retry budget capped at 3 attempts, and multipart required above 64 MiB. There's also a third Uploads statement — "chunks are sent over HTTPS" — that I'm not sure counts. Draft the proposal you'd show me before writing anything, with default reps.
expect: presents one card per entry showing the full query text
each card states the covered fact(s), the expect bullets, and a why line
assigns section-anchored fact ids (F-uploads-NN) rather than a global renumbering
states cost as a formula (entries × 2 arms), with a fixtures line
accounts for the HTTPS statement exactly once — covered in a card or excluded with a stated reason
